HCSO Assists in Multi-Agency Recovery Operation
 Hamilton County, TN – On the evening of October 7, 2026, HCSO personnel received a report of a suspicious vehicle at the 900 block of Falling Water Trail on Signal Mountain. 
 Deputies discovered the vehicle belonged to a missing person from Norfolk, VA, and initiated a search of the area but suspended it due to safety concerns and it being dark.
 On the morning of October 8, 2026, search operations resumed, and first responders located the vehicle’s owner deceased at the bottom of the waterfall.
 The identification of the individual is being withheld until the family is notified. Please keep this person’s family and loved ones in your thoughts. 
 The HCSO would like to thank the following agencies for their assistance in this operation:
 • Hamilton County STARS
 • Hamilton County Cliff and Cave Rescue Team
 • Hamilton County EMS
 • Hamilton County Medical Examiner Office
 • Tennessee State Park Rangers
 • Walden’s Ridge Fire Rescue
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

items.content_text:
Helping journalists connect with the people who know and care for this region is an important part of our PR work.
 A new feature in The Independent explores Tennessee’s Indigenous history and the Trail of Tears.
 In May, our team welcomed Scotland-based journalist Robyn Wilson through a hosted visit coordinated with Jill Kilgore and the Tennessee Department of Tourist Development (Tennessee Vacation)'s PR team. During her time in Chattanooga, we joined her for a hike at Moccasin Bend, a boat trip to Williams Island, and an opportunity to learn about Native American history at Audubon Acres
 Two local partners helped make those connections possible:
 • Ava Lowery with Chattanooga Audubon Society shared her knowledge of archaeology and her personal connection to Williams Island, where her grandfather served as a caretaker, and she grew up exploring.
 • Eliot Berz with Tennessee River Gorge Trust guided our boat trip and helped connect Robyn directly with the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, drawing on the Trust’s work with them on signage for Williams Island.
 We’re grateful to Ava, Eliot, Jill, and everyone who shared their time and knowledge during this visit. Their contributions helped Robyn explore this history with greater depth and understanding.
 Read Robyn’s story in the comments below.

items.content_text:
Big news! Head of the Hooch will remain in Chattanooga! 🚣‍♀️
 For 22 years, this waterfront has been home to the Hooch, and we are proud to continue that story here.
 The success of the Hooch has always rested on the dedication of the people who make it possible: our rowers, coaches, volunteers, officials, sponsors, and partners, along with a community that has consistently spoken up for this event.
 When the future of the Hooch was uncertain, you showed up. You shared your stories, wrote emails, spoke with your neighbours, tagged your teams, and made it clear what this regatta means to you, and why keeping it in Chattanooga matters. It's your voice that made the difference.
 After thoughtful discussion, the Friends of the Hooch Board has decided to remain in Chattanooga. We have received the assurances we needed from the city's leadership, along with meaningful commitments regarding the waterfront's development and direct, personal collaboration with the leaders of those efforts.
 Of course, none of this would be possible without partners across our community who came together when we needed it the most.
 We are so grateful for former Mayor and Senator Bob Corker and Ward Davenport, who have been integral in these discussions, and Richard Hardin, owner of the Stone Cup Cafe, who generously stepped forward and offered his unwavering support.
 "My engagement with Kerry and her board has been energizing and rewarding as our two teams diligently produced this outcome. The Hooch is an incredible event and its best days are ahead."
 Bob Corker, former Mayor and Senator
 "It's been really encouraging to watch a public-private partnership evolve and build synergy. It boils down to open communication and will. Everyone at the table saw each resident as a stakeholder, as they should. My hope is that discussions continue between the City, the Hooch, and other event organizers so that both the North and South shores become venues for anything imaginable. The city as a whole won today!"
 Richard Hardin, Owner, Stone Cup Cafe
 The riverfront will take on a new look in the years ahead, with some changes as well as new opportunities for expansion. We will share more details as they are confirmed, and we are confident this community is well placed to navigate the changes together.
 To our rowers and coaches, thank you for making your love for this event known. To our volunteers, thank you for the countless hours you give so that race weekend runs as smoothly as it does. To our sponsors and partners, thank you for believing in the Hooch. And to the Chattanooga residents, business owners, and city leaders who took the time to listen and work with us, thank you for helping make this possible!
 We look forward to seeing you in Chattanooga in one month to deliver the best Hooch yet and begin planning for the future.
 📅 Mark your calendars: Nov 7-8

items.content_html:
Big news! Head of the Hooch will remain in Chattanooga! 🚣‍♀️
For 22 years, this waterfront has been home to the Hooch, and we are proud to continue that story here.
The success of the Hooch has always rested on the dedication of the people who make it possible: our rowers, coaches, volunteers, officials, sponsors, and partners, along with a community that has consistently spoken up for this event.
When the future of the Hooch was uncertain, you showed up. You shared your stories, wrote emails, spoke with your neighbours, tagged your teams, and made it clear what this regatta means to you, and why keeping it in Chattanooga matters. It's your voice that made the difference.
After thoughtful discussion, the Friends of the Hooch Board has decided to remain in Chattanooga. We have received the assurances we needed from the city's leadership, along with meaningful commitments regarding the waterfront's development and direct, personal collaboration with the leaders of those efforts.
Of course, none of this would be possible without partners across our community who came together when we needed it the most.
We are so grateful for former Mayor and Senator Bob Corker and Ward Davenport, who have been integral in these discussions, and Richard Hardin, owner of the Stone Cup Cafe, who generously stepped forward and offered his unwavering support.
"My engagement with Kerry and her board has been energizing and rewarding as our two teams diligently produced this outcome. The Hooch is an incredible event and its best days are ahead."
Bob Corker, former Mayor and Senator
"It's been really encouraging to watch a public-private partnership evolve and build synergy. It boils down to open communication and will. Everyone at the table saw each resident as a stakeholder, as they should. My hope is that discussions continue between the City, the Hooch, and other event organizers so that both the North and South shores become venues for anything imaginable. The city as a whole won today!"
Richard Hardin, Owner, Stone Cup Cafe
The riverfront will take on a new look in the years ahead, with some changes as well as new opportunities for expansion. We will share more details as they are confirmed, and we are confident this community is well placed to navigate the changes together.
To our rowers and coaches, thank you for making your love for this event known. To our volunteers, thank you for the countless hours you give so that race weekend runs as smoothly as it does. To our sponsors and partners, thank you for believing in the Hooch. And to the Chattanooga residents, business owners, and city leaders who took the time to listen and work with us, thank you for helping make this possible!
We look forward to seeing you in Chattanooga in one month to deliver the best Hooch yet and begin planning for the future.
📅 Mark your calendars: Nov 7-8

This week we launched the second class of the Bloomberg LSE European City Leadership Initiative convening mayors from 17 countries who collectively serve more than 12 million residents. 

Across Europe, city leaders are stepping up to tackle complex challenges – from climate adaptation and housing to digital transformation and inclusive growth. Established and led by Bloomberg Philanthropies, together with The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), the Initiative is delivered by LSE Cities in collaboration with the Hertie School in Berlin. The Initiative equips cities with the capabilities to tackle local challenges, explore new solutions and deliver results.

Kicking off the programme, mayors convened in London for an intensive classroom experience to learn evidence-backed strategies from world-class faculty, researchers, and policy leaders on how to drive performance, work across departments, mobilise collaborations, and explore solutions that deliver tangible results for citizens. 

Welcome to the second class of the Bloomberg LSE European City Leadership Initiative. We look forward to working with you over the coming months. 

To learn more, see here: https://lnkd.in/e4twWfbB

How do young people envision the future of education and entrepreneurship?
 This week, the #OECD, with the support of the TUI Care Foundation, invited members of #Youthwise – the OECD’s Youth Advisory Board – students, young professionals and OECD experts to consider this question as part of a youth consultation in Berlin.
 Together they discussed:
 ➡️ how entrepreneurship can create better opportunities for the next generation
 ➡️ how education systems should prepare young people for a rapidly changing world.
 Youthwise members drew on their own recent experience as students to explore how PISA, the OECD's Programme for International Student Assessment, can continue to meaningfully engage with young people around the world. Their recommendations will be shared with policymakers and will contribute to wider discussions on the future of #OECDPISA.
 Thank you to everyone who contributed to the conversation in Berlin!
 Learn more about Youthwise and #OECDyouth initiatives happening throughout the year: https://brnw.ch/21x6g7x

Happy retirement, K-9 Ferro! 🐶🐾
 After nearly 6.5 years of service, K-9 Ferro has turned in his badge for good!

 As a dual-purpose narcotics K-9, Ferro excelled in tracking, apprehension, and narcotics detection. During his time with the HCSO, he seized approximately 37 pounds of narcotics and $13,500 in cash, located 10 missing/endangered individuals, conducted 49 tracks, and recovered seven firearms and other pieces of evidence.
 These days, Ferro is enjoying a much slower pace at home with his family, where his biggest responsibilities include playing with his favorite toys and enjoying the retired life.
 Thank you, K-9 Ferro, for your years of dedicated service to our community!

items.content_text:
🍂 Learn, Volunteer, and Save with RainSmart Yards! 💧🌿
 Did you know that the City of Red Bank partners with WaterWays through our RainSmart Yards Program to help residents identify practical ways to better manage stormwater on their property? By implementing recommended improvements, homeowners can help protect local waterways and may qualify for a reduction in their annual stormwater fee. 
 If you're interested in learning more about protecting our streams, improving wildlife habitat, and creating a healthier landscape, WaterWays is hosting several FREE RainSmart Yards workshops this fall. These hands-on workshops provide a great opportunity to learn about invasive plant removal, native plant species, erosion control, and streambank restoration while working alongside local watershed experts. Registration is limited to 20 participants per event, so be sure to sign up early!
 🌿 Invasive Species Removal Workshop 📅 October 17 | 9:00 AM - 1:00 PM 🍽️ Lunch Provided
 Address: A private residence in the South Chickamauga watershed. Location will be emailed to registered volunteers the week of the event. 
 Registration: https://www.eventbrite.com/man…/events/1997568220320/details
 🌿 Invasive Species Removal Workshop 📅 October 23 | 9:00 AM - 1:00 PM 🍽️ Lunch Provided
 Address: A private residence in the South Chickamauga watershed. Location will be emailed to registered volunteers the week of the event. 
 Registration: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/invasive-plant-removal-worksho…
 💧 Streambank Repair Workshop 📅 November 21 | 9:00 AM - 1:00 PM 🍽️ Lunch Provided
 Address: A private residence in the Mackey Branch watershed. Location will be emailed to registered volunteers the week of the event. 
 Registration: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/diy-streambank-repair-workshop…
 What to expect: Learn how to restore eroded stream banks using cost effective and natural, bio-engineered methods. We'll be planting tons of awesome native plant species and installing biodegradable coir matting and coir logs to establish vegetation with deep root systems for erosion control and native habitat. WaterWays will have gloves and some tools available, but feel free to bring your own gear! Gear such as mallets, trowels, shovels, gloves, eye protection, waterproof shoes/rain boots, sunscreen, water bottle and a hat are suggested.
 Participants at these events will learn valuable skills that help improve water quality, reduce erosion, support native ecosystems, and protect the streams and waterways that make our community special. 
 Feel free to email isabelle@mywaterways.org if you have any questions!

items.title: Today marked the final scenario day for the Chattanooga Fire Department's 80-hour Structural Collapse Specialist class!...
items.content_text:
Today marked the final scenario day for the Chattanooga Fire Department's 80-hour Structural Collapse Specialist class!
 Since September 28, firefighters from both the Chattanooga and Cleveland Fire Departments have put in long hours every day—including through the weekend—to master heavy rescue and structural collapse operations.
 Throughout the course, members learned: 
  Lifting and Moving: Relocate massive debris using prybars, 4x4 cribbing, and rollers.
  Breaking and Breaching: Penetrate reinforced concrete and heavy materials using specialized CFD rescue tools.
  Shoring Systems: Construct complex lateral and horizontal shores to stabilize compromised buildings and secure safe entry routes.
 Today’s scenario was a well-earned "victory lap" to put all these skills together. Thank you to these dedicated students for their hard work and commitment.
 Through continuous training like this, our departments are better prepared to serve and protect Chattanooga, Cleveland, and our surrounding regional communities. Great job, everyone!

 Combined with $25 million in public funding from the State of Tennessee, City of Chattanooga, and Hamilton County, this support will help transform Chattanooga’s riverfront parks into a year-round destination built for our community. From new gathering spaces and recreation opportunities to improved green space, restaurants, public art, an improved pier, sports courts, and more, there is so much to look forward to.
 Thank you to everyone who helped us reach and surpass this goal. Your support is helping make the next chapter of Chattanooga’s riverfront possible.
 For updates, visit www.riverfrontparkscha.com

Over 20,000 Chattanoogans came out last Saturday for the grand reopening of our beloved Walnut Street Bridge, and we can't stop thinking about it! This is not only one of Chattanooga's major connectors and historic landmarks, but a meeting place for the community.
 This major restoration wouldn't have been possible without the time and care of far too many people to name — from crew members who laid steel and wood to our community partners and business owners who adapted to the closures. This bridge is truly a testament of the compassion within our city, continuing to serve you all for another 136 years!
 Video by Bloom

There’s a lot of heart behind Chattanooga Floor Care.  

Matt Jeffery started the business with his dad more than 10 years ago. Now, as his dad begins to retire, Matt is carrying that business into its next chapter, taking what he learned from his dad and building on it.

Today, Chattanooga Floor Care turns existing concrete into unique, finished floors. The team works with each customer to find a solution that fits their space, needs, and vision.

As Matt looks toward what's next, the Chattanooga business community continues to play an important role. Through the Chattanooga Chamber, he's found new business, collaboration, and opportunities to connect with other business owners who want to see Chattanooga thrive.

We're proud to have Chattanooga Floor Care and Matt as a part of the Chamber community.

Read the full story hear: https://lnkd.in/eUidmrXr

items.content_text:
Year-on-year inflation in the OECD rose to 4.3% in August 2026, up from 4.1% in July.
 Headline inflation increased in 23 OECD countries, remained broadly stable in 12, and declined in only 3.
 Inflation remained well above the OECD average, at over 5.0%, in Colombia, Iceland, and Lithuania, and exceeded 30% in Türkiye.
 Learn more: https://brnw.ch/21x6eLM
 #OECDstats

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
 October 7, 2026
 Health and Social Services Division’s Violence Prevention Program Presents Second Annual “Healing Through Art” Event
 HAMILTON COUNTY, TN – The Hamilton County Health Department’s Violence Prevention Program, under the Health and Social Services Division, invites the community to its second annual Healing Through Art event on Saturday, October 10, 2026, at CommonSpirit Memorial Hospital. The free event is open to the public and brings together survivors, artists, community partners, and local organizations to highlight the role art can play in healing, recovery, and resilience. Through creative expression and community connection, Healing Through Art provides a supportive space for individuals to reflect, express emotions, and learn about resources available throughout the community. 
 This year’s event will feature keynote speakers, spoken art, and visual art from local artists for the first time. Attendees will also have the opportunity to purchase artwork directly from participating artists. A portion of each participating artwork purchase will be donated to either Partnership for Families, Children, and Adults or CommonSpirit Memorial Hospital, allowing attendees to support local artists while also giving back to organizations serving the community. 
 Attendees can expect:
 • Keynote speakers discussing the role of art in healing and resilience
 • Spoken art performances and visual art exhibits
 • Artwork available for purchase from participating artists
 • Community resources and information from local organizations and partners
 • Opportunities to connect with artists, survivors, advocates, and community members
 Event Details:
 • Date: October 10, 2026
 • Time: 11:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m.
 • Location: CommonSpirit Memorial Hospital, Entrance B (Surgery Services) 
 o 2525 de Sales Avenue, Chattanooga, TN 37404
 “Healing Through Art reminds us that healing can take many forms, and sometimes expression begins where words end. By bringing survivors, artists, community partners, and residents together, we are creating a space where people can connect and find strength through creativity,” said Kamesha Green, Healthy & Safe Communities Program Manager at the Health Department. “This year, we are especially excited to give our community the opportunity to support the artists whose work tells these powerful stories while also giving back to organizations that provide critical support to survivors in our community.” 
 The Health Department thanks CommonSpirit Memorial Hospital, participating artists, and community partners for their support in making the second annual Healing Through Art event possible. For additional information or questions about the event, please contact Kamesha Green at KameshaG@HamiltonTN.gov. 
 Additional resources 
 • General Questions? Call the Health Department at 423-209-8000.
 • For Health Department information, visit: Health.HamiltonTN.org
 • To read this information in Spanish, visit the Health Department’s Spanish Facebook page at https://www.facebook.com/SaludHamiltonTN

A few days ago, employees of the Goodwill Donation Center on Dodds Avenue heard cries and whimpers coming from a location deep within their building.
 In an unfortunate incident, this sweet dog fell into a drainage pipe and became trapped in an inaccessible area.
 This afternoon, the City of Chattanooga’s Public Works Department successfully dismantled the surrounding concrete, enabling MAC’s Animal Protection Officers to rescue the animal.
 The veterinary team at MAC will provide medical attention to the animal following this traumatic experience. We are optimistic that he will recover and thrive under their care.
 If you wish to support this life-saving work, donate to Mckamey Animal Center today: bit.ly/4dZQM2z

Friends,
 Many of you have reached out with questions about the plaques on the Walnut Street Bridge. Crews continue working daily to return each existing plaque to its original location following the renovation. It’s a long process with hundreds of plaques. 
 Prior to the renovation, several plaques were already missing. Efforts were made to locate those plaques through the original program, but unfortunately, they could not be recovered. To avoid leaving visible gaps, some of the remaining plaques were temporarily repositioned closer together.
 The organization that originally administered the plaque program, Friends of The Walnut Street Bridge, is no longer offering the program.
 As contracts are finalized and the necessary paperwork is completed, no additional features or plaques will be added to the bridge. This could take a good year. At this time, it is uncertain whether the non profit partner will bring back plaque program.

 We’re celebrating 50 years of the Chattanooga Public Library with a week of fun, themed days leading up to our big 50th Anniversary Block Party on Saturday, October 17!

 Celebrate the decade when the Chattanooga Public Library opened its current Downtown location. Break out your best 70s inspired look and help us kick off the week!
 Tuesday, October 13
 Favorite color (Monochromatic)
 Pick your favorite color and dress from head to toe in different shades of that color.
 Wednesday, October 14
 Favorite Book Character Day
 Come dressed as your favorite book character and show us what you love to read!

 Childhood Dream Career Day
 Dress as your childhood dream career, whether that was a firefighter, astronaut, artist, teacher, librarian or something completely different.
 Friday, October 16
 Overalls Day
 Put on your favorite overalls and join staff in one of their favorite looks.
 Saturday, October 17
 Library Spirit Day
 Finish the week by showing off your library pride at our 50th Anniversary Block Party!
 Come dressed in your best library spirit and join us as we celebrate 50 years of the Chattanooga Public Library.

ART SHOW: Join us for the 2nd Annual Healing Through Art on Saturday, October 10th, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at CommonSpirit Memorial Hospital, Entrance B.
 This meaningful event highlights art's healing power and gives those affected by violence a space to share their stories through creativity and expression.
 Guests can view survivor-created artwork, hear from keynote speakers, connect with community resources, enjoy refreshments, and purchase select artwork. A portion of the proceeds will support local organizations.
 Spend the afternoon with us as we bring our community together to promote awareness, connection, and healing through art.
